Units: Count Valid dimensions: * Source ARN * Flow ARN * Availability Zone * All flows |\\\\n| `SourceARQRequests` | The number of retransmitted packets that were requested through automatic repeat request (ARQ) and received. This metric applies to sources that use the RIST, Zixi, or SRT protocol. It doesn\\'t apply to flows that receive content from an entitlement. Units: Count Valid dimensions: * Source ARN * Flow ARN * Availability Zone * All flows |\\\\n| `SourceBitRate` | The bitrate of the incoming (source) video. Units: bits per second (bps) Valid dimensions: * Source ARN * Flow ARN * Availability Zone * All flows **Note:** Both MediaConnect and the Zixi protocol use bandwidth optimization techniques that can affect bitrate measurements: * In flows with Zixi sources, Zixi often optimizes network usage by substituting repetitive content packets with null packets. * For entitlements, MediaConnect performs similar optimization between the content originator\\'s flow and the subscriber\\'s flow. For example, in a 30 Mbps stream with repetitive content (like a black slate), either optimization might reduce the bitrate to 5 Mbps. These bitrate fluctuations are normal and don\\'t affect content quality, but they might be noticeable in your bitrate monitoring. A value of 1 indicates that the source is connected and a value of 0 (zero) indicates that the source is disconnected. This metric applies only to sources that use the Zixi or SRT protocol. This redundancy helps to minimize disruption to your video stream. To use source\\\\nfailover, you specify two sources for the flow, then choose\\\\none of two options for the failover mode: *Merge* or *Failover*.\\\\n\\\\n* Merge mode combines the sources into a single stream, allowing a graceful\\\\n recovery from any single-source loss. If you set the failover mode to *Merge*, you can set the recovery window, which is\\\\n the size of the buffer (delay) that you want MediaConnect to maintain. A larger\\\\n recovery window means a longer delay in transmitting the stream, but more room\\\\n for error correction. A smaller recovery window means a shorter delay, but less\\\\n room for error correction. The ST 2022-7 standard defines a\\\\n method that replaces missing packets with packets in an identical, redundant\\\\n stream. This type of failover requires a small latency buffer in your\\\\n workflow to allow time for MediaConnect to recover packets from the two\\\\n streams.\\\\n* Failover mode allows switching between a primary and a backup stream. This\\\\n switching facilitates an easy transition to a more reliable stream. If you set\\\\n the failover mode to *Failover*, you can\\\\n specify a source as the primary source. The second source serves as the backup.\\\\n If you don\u2019t specify a primary source, MediaConnect treats both sources with\\\\n equal priority, and switches to the available source as needed.\\\\n\\\\nMediaConnect uses the two modes of failover in the following ways:\\\\n\\\\n* In the *Merge* mode, MediaConnect uses content from\\\\n both sources. The flow randomly selects one of the sources to start with. If\\\\n that source is missing a packet\\\\n\\\\n*[truncated \u2014 additional content omitted]*\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/mediaconnect/latest/ug/source-failover.html\"},{\"rank_order\":3,\"title\":\"Troubleshooting SRT and Zixi with AWS Elemental MediaConnect | AWS for M&E Blog\",\"context\":\"### MediaConnect receiver recommendations\\\\n\\\\n**Do not set a primary source for failover *unless* the secondary is known to be lower in quality or reliability**. {"id": "da1e9ea9-0420-4185-97b8-a47e11e1fd5a", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "This pattern points to signal/encoding-level corruption at the source rather than a network transport problem — most consistent with an issue on the AWS Elemental Link device or its upstream feed (e.g., encoder hiccup, unstable camera/input signal, HDMI/SDI handshake issue, or a problem on the Link's local encode pipeline) rather than packet loss in transit.

**Why:**
- **PCR (Program Clock Reference) errors** indicate timing/clock discontinuities in the transport stream itself — this happens when the encoder's own clock or multiplexing is unstable, not when packets are merely dropped on the wire.
- **Continuity counter errors** mean TS packets are arriving out of sequence or being duplicated/skipped at the source encoding level.
- **SourceBitRate drops** show the encoder itself is producing less data momentarily (e.g., scene complexity change, encoder stall, or signal dropout at the Link's input) rather than data being lost after it was sent.

**The metric that separates this from network loss: `SourceConnected` staying at 1 combined with `SourceDisconnections` staying at 0.**

If this were a network/transport loss issue (lost UDP/RTP packets, path congestion, Zixi/SRT retransmission exhaustion), you'd typically expect to see the connection itself degrade or drop — `SourceConnected` flipping to 0, `SourceDisconnections` incrementing, or (for Zixi/SRT/RIST sources) a spike in `SourceARQRequests`/`SourceARQRecovered` or `SourceNotRecoveredPackets` as the protocol tries to repair transport-level loss. Since the connection stays up and intact the whole time, the stream is reaching MediaConnect fine — the corruption is already baked into the stream before it leaves the source, pointing at the Elemental Link encoder or its upstream feed rather than the network path.

If you want, I can look at this against a real flow's CloudWatch metrics to confirm the pattern on your setup.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
